messages:
amanda: Hey all — Helios Health wants to run a Private deployment POC next week. Key asks from their network/security team:
- static egress IPs per region for allowlisting
- preserve client source IP or at least have a reliable X-Forwarded-For
- they MUST do TLS inspection and SNI rewrite on their side (corporate TLS bridge), but they asked if Redwood can do SNI rewrite or mTLS termination on our connector instead
- confirm firewall ports/FQDNs + any NAT hairpin needs

liam: Thanks Amanda. Short answers: we can provide static egress IPs for Private (extra charge per EIP/region) and we can surface X-Forwarded-For for proxied requests. We do NOT currently offer on-the-fly SNI rewrite in our hosted edge; that normally lives in the customer's TLS bridge or an L7 edge. For mTLS: our connector can be configured to require client certs (mutual TLS) on Private installs, but hosted customers usually terminate mTLS at the customer gateway. :thinking:

jess: Network checklist (quick):
```
# Allow outbound to Redwood endpoints (example IPs/FQDNs)
- 13.52.100.200/32 TCP 443 -> redwood-api-us.example.com
- 3.210.45.12/32 TCP 443 -> redwood-connector-us.example.com
# Ephemeral return ports for TCP: 1024-65535 (NAT return)
# If using PrivateLink (interface endpoint): allow HTTPS to the interface ENI IPs in the subnet
```
If customer insists on SNI rewrite, they need to rewrite SNI to match the cert at our endpoint or terminate + re-encrypt to us. If they terminate to inspect, our TLS must be the downstream hop.

mike-sre: Pricing note: static EIP assignment for Private deployments is an add-on. Estimate: $200/month per reserved EIP + egress metering. If they need geo-redundant egress (us-west + eu-west) that's two EIPs. Also: dedicated capacity changes SLA and price band. Amanda — can you capture expected TPS and average token/day? We'll need it for a reserved capacity quote. :money_with_wings:

amanda: Customer answer to bandwidth: baseline 50 rps peak, 15M tokens/day. They said security questionnaire lists: certificate rotation cadence, KMS/HSM usage, packet capture retention policy, and evidence of TLS cipher suites supported. Also they asked if we can preserve original client IP through PrivateLink (they want source IP in logs for forensics).

liam: PrivateLink preserves source IP for traffic that flows directly to the interface endpoint inside the customer's VPC (our service runs in their VPC via interface endpoint), but depending on the connector topology we may still see NAT. For absolute preservation, the recommended pattern is:
1) Customer creates interface endpoint + security group that allows their ingress
2) Our connector runs in a subnet with source_dest_check disabled and we can surface client IP via proxy protocol or X-Forwarded-For
If they must inspect TLS and rewrite SNI: two options:
- Option A: Customer TLS bridge rewrites SNI and forwards to our endpoint (customer-managed) — simplest for them
- Option B: Customer terminates -> inspection -> re-encrypts to our endpoint (we see client cert as new client) -> we can still require mTLS from their re-encrypting proxy

jess: Workaround we use for similar customers: ask them to insert an L7 proxy in front that handles SNI rewrite and mTLS termination, then forward to PrivateLink. That keeps our surface unchanged and meets most compliance checks. Example SG rules they should add: allow inbound from corp-proxy CIDR -> interface endpoint ENI on 443, deny other subnets. :shield:

netops-bot: Checklist created: POC-NETWORK-3339998888:
- Confirm EIP count & regions
- Provide FTPS/FQDN allowlist (we provided examples)
- Confirm TPS & token/day for pricing
- Security questionnaire items assigned to security team

amanda: OK — I'll get Helios to confirm whether they'll run SNI rewrite on their TLS bridge or expect us to. Also sending TPS/token numbers to Mike. Will follow up with their SOC about cert rotation/KMS requirements. Thanks! :thumbsup:
